source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Melanose and stem-end rot (ជម្ងឺ Melanose និង Stem-End Rot, caused by Diaporthe citri / Phomopsis citri) is a fungal disease that shows on leaves, twigs, and fruit as small, raised, dark brown to black scab-like spots with a rough, sandpaper-like texture; on fruit these spots are mainly cosmetic but reduce market grade, while on twigs the same fungus causes dieback of dead wood, which becomes the main source of spores that reinfect new growth during wet weather.

The disease is closely linked to stem-end rot after harvest: the fungus can infect the fruit stem/button and lie dormant, only causing visible rot at the stem end after the fruit is picked and in storage, which makes dead twig material in the canopy an important hidden source of post-harvest losses even when the standing fruit looks fine at harvest.

Control focuses on removing dead wood (the main spore source) through regular pruning, improving air circulation in the canopy to speed drying after rain, and applying copper fungicide/Bordeaux mixture sprays timed to protect new flush and young fruit during wet periods; careful, gentle harvesting that avoids tearing the stem button also reduces stem-end rot losses after picking.
